failure_modes: Assay/signal floor in low‑biomass lavage or CSF prevents discrimination between senescence conditions despite valid in‑vitro differences (spike‑in recovery insufficient or variable).

Species‑ or administration‑specific delivery barriers (e.g., nasal retention, mucociliary clearance, scale differences) overwhelm any source‑cell advantage so that favorable in‑vitro signatures do not increase in vivo recoverability (false inference of no causal link).

Labeling, capture, or fractionation artifacts (including co‑purifying non‑vesicular particles or loss of fragile EV subpopulations during processing) create apparent senescence‑linked differences in orthogonal analytics that are in fact processing artifacts (false positive causal attribution).

Donor heterogeneity, upstream culture variables (media, oxygen), or downstream purification batch effects covary with induced senescence conditions and drive observed differences, so senescence mechanism is a correlated but non‑causal marker (confounding).

Operationalizing senescence thresholds (p16/p21, SASP panel) is unreliable or not reproducible across donors, making the proposed gate non‑actionable for manufacturing (unmeasurable or non‑generalizable).

Favorable source‑cell states that pass the proposed gate yield insufficient EV quantity or unacceptable manufacturing tradeoffs, so the attribute cannot be adopted even if analytically predictive (manufacturability blockade).

Negative large‑animal biodistribution evidence suggests intranasal recoverability in rodents may not predict primate or human CNS exposure, so the in vivo bridge remains uninformative for clinical translation (translational confounding).
strongest_objection: The single strongest bounded reason this proposal could fail is that intranasal delivery and short‑interval recoverability are dominated by delivery-, formulation-, species-, or sampling‑limitations rather than by source‑cell senescence effects on EV integrity; thus even if senescence alters orthogonal in vitro EV signatures, those differences will not translate into reproducible in vivo recoverable signal (or will be undetectable) in the relevant short‑interval lavage/CSF/olfactory compartments, producing a false negative for the central causal claim.
